stories.headline: USMNT players are beefing online again: A look at the most memorable, pettiest feuds
stories.summary: A new argument between USMNT players has caused a stir, continuing a long tradition of American stars beefing for no reason.
stories.body:
Death, taxes, and current/former U.S. men's national team players publicly starting quarrels.

It seems as though the American soccer scene can't go through long stretches without a high-profile figure starting a beef, and on Thursday, retired striker Eddie Johnson caused a stir after calling out national team legend Landon Donovan.

"You talk so much s--- about every other young upcoming player in the past but yourself lol why don't we talk about the 5 years you were in Germany and failed and ran back to MLS bc you weren't good enough? Why don't we speak about this?" Johnson wrote on social media, with a screenshot to a quote from Donovan, who discussed the growing excitement over up-and-coming star Cavan Sullivan.

Donovan pointed out former prodigy Freddy Adu, as well as Johnson, as part of his argument to calm expectations.

"One of the best considerably players in our country failed in Europe early in his career," Johnson continued. "No one killed him but he's killing all these young players that have done more then he ever has done in Europe."

This kind of spicy-but-ridiculous online drama is nothing new for the USMNT.

The lore of public and unnecessary beefs involving the USMNT is like a tradition. In an attempt to highlight some of the previous chapters -- sticking to the silliest and most pointless beefs rather than the more serious ones -- we've made a short list of some memorable incidents.

Landon Donovan vs. Christian Pulisic: 'It's pissing me off'

This isn't the first time Donovan appears on this list -- and it won't be the last, either.

After star player Christian Pulisic asked to take the summer off during the 2025 Gold Cup, Donovan called out USMNT players who missed the tournament.

"This is what it means to represent your country," Donovan said of Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo while working as a pundit during the UEFA Nations League final.

"Forty years old. He's played a long-ass season. He's tired. He's out there grinding. Hurt himself in the process, and I can't help but think about some of our guys on vacation, not wanting to play in the Gold Cup. It's pissing me off."

Pulisic's father responded on social media by posting ChatGPT's explanation for Donovan's 144-day sabbatical in 2012-13 that later saw him left out of the 2014 World Cup squad.

"Landon Donovan took his sabbatical because he was feeling both physically and mentally exhausted after years of intense competition and the pressure that comes with being a top athlete," read a screenshot that included the AI text.

Pulisic hit "like" on the post.

Jermaine Jones vs. Jordan Morris: 'Really? Why you go the easy way?'

Justifiably flustered after the USMNT's failure to qualify for the 2018 World Cup, midfielder Jermaine Jones, who had recently been left off the national team roster, shared his complaints about the U.S. team on Instagram Live.

While criticizing players who never take a chance abroad in Europe, Jones specifically put a spotlight on Seattle Sounders forward Jordan Morris, saying that Morris turned down an opportunity to play in Germany.

According to Jones, Morris told him: "I want to go home. My dad is a doctor in Seattle, and my mom, they bought me and my girlfriend a dog."

"Really?" said Jones during the livestream. "Why you go the easy way when you have the chance?"

Morris has since said that the dog was not a factor, saying: "I obviously didn't stay in Seattle because of a dog."

Alejandro Bedoya vs. Jozy Altidore: 'You have a lot to say but never to anyone's face'

After USMNT teammates Alejandro Bedoya and Jozy Altidore faced off in an MLS match in 2017, Bedoya was asked postgame whether a penalty decision for Altidore was correct.

"Knowing him, he tends to go down easily in the box," Bedoya said just weeks before a national team camp. "So, just leave it at that."

That didn't sit well with Altidore, who took to social media.

"Nice comment pal," he wrote. "You have a lot to say but never to anyones face. Im surprised.. but I shouldn't be."

Both later downplayed the back-and-forth, but it was still clear that Bedoya had struck a nerve.

Eric Wynalda vs. Landon Donovan: 'There's a big part of me that wants to stuff a sock in your mouth right now'

Last year, Donovan gained attention after he said that rising star Diego Luna should remain in MLS, and not move to Europe just yet, to cement a place for the USMNT's 2026 World Cup roster.

It was an eyebrow-raising comment, which provoked former striker Eric Wynalda to rant about Donovan's advice during his "Unleashed with Eric Wynalda" show.

"Stop polluting minds because it's getting f---ing annoying. Nobody believes that, Landon," Wynalda said. "Nobody even comes close to believing that this place is the best place to get ready for a World Cup.

"I don't want to get into these fights, but there's a big part of me that wants to stuff a sock in your mouth right now. It's getting annoying as hell."

Wynalda has previously noted that he has "never been friends" with Donovan. Big surprise!

Tim Weah vs. former USMNT players: 'I just feel like they're really evil'

Let's go back to when Pulisic took a break during the 2025 Gold Cup.

It occurred during the filming of the "Pulisic" documentary, which highlighted the criticism that the current national team was receiving from former national team players about the squad's performances and the commitment of someone like Pulisic.

"I think those guys are chasing checks and, for me, I just feel like they're really evil," Pulisic's teammate Tim Weah said in the documentary. "They've been players, and they know what it's like when you're getting bashed. Those are the same guys that'll turn around and shake your hand and try to be friendly with you at the end of the day."

Weah later stood by his comments after being asked whether he regretted them.

stories.headline: UCL Matchday 2: Viking FK and PSG impress; Man United a mess
stories.summary: The Chaaaaaampions! Europe's top competition returned with a ton of goals, a ton of big results and plenty to talk about. Let's start with the tiny Norwegian team that gave Bayern Munich a fright.
stories.body:
It is the way of the soccer world right now that competitions must get larger, with more teams, more matches per team and a much lower average reading on the jeopardy per match scale.

Aside from the obvious wear-and-tear concerns, I don't really mind this development. (Maybe it's the American in me: I'm used to bloat.)

I don't mind that the Euros have 24 teams, or that the Champions League has 36, or that the World Cup has 48 -- and that two-thirds of the competitors reach the knockout rounds in all of these tournaments. That has allowed for super-cool stories to develop.

Ukraine snuck into the knockout rounds at Euro 2020 (amid growing geopolitical stress) and then upset Sweden. Slovenia and Slovakia eked out advancement in 2024, too, and nearly pulled upsets. And while a huge Champions League with a huge set of knockout rounds has allowed more time for struggling powers like PSG and Manchester City in 2024-25 to rebound from poor starts, it also allowed Bodø/Glimt to find their footing and eventually take down Manchester City, Atlético Madrid and Inter Milan, consecutively, while nearly making the quarterfinals last season.

I don't mind bloat as long as it allows for proper storytelling and extra world-building. In a world with tilted finances, where only a few teams are actually capable of winning the whole thing, a fun journey almost matters more than the eventual destination.

Matchday 1 of this year's Champions League concerned me a bit in that regard. There was still fun to be had -- Como ran away from RB Leipzig in their first ever European group stage game, Real Madrid outlasted Inter Milan in a battle of European royalty, and 11 of 18 matches featured at least four goals. Goals are fun.

- UCL Talking Points: Who's to blame for Man United mess?

- Reaction: Man City can't compete with gold standard PSG

- Kirkland: Real Madrid did win, but glory feels far away

Still, Davids weren't exactly scoring damage points on Goliaths. PSG, Barcelona and Bayern Munich beat Slovan Bratislava, Feyenoord and Bodø/Glimt by a combined 16-2, and debutants LASK, Sabah and Viking all lost by a combined 8-1. It was a foreboding start, a sign that maybe Europe's giants have even further distanced themselves from the pack. I'm a fan of storytelling, and that's the least fun story to tell.

Luckily, Matchday 2 gave us delightful plot twists and track meets.

It also took us to Norway.

Main characters of the week

No. 1: Viking FK

Viking FK has lived a full club life since its founding in Stavanger in 1899: Early regional titles in the 1920s and 1930s; national titles in the 1950s, when that became a thing to aspire to; great spells (four straight titles in the 1970s); poor spells (relegation in 1986 and 2017); the requisite financial overextension in the 2010s (who among us).

On occasion, they've also enjoyed the glory of home European nights. They hosted Borussia Mönchengladbach (and drew 1-1) in the 1979-80 UEFA Cup, held Barcelona to a 0-0 draw in qualification for the inaugural 1992-93 Champions League) and walloped Sporting CP and drew with Werder Bremen in the 1999-2000 UEFA Cup. And in maybe the most famous night of the old Stavanger Stadion, they thumped Chelsea 4-2 in the 2002-03 UEFA Cup despite goals from Frank Lampard and John Terry.

Their current home, Viking Stadion, saw a win over Monaco in the 2005-06 UEFA Cup, plus a couple of fun victories in the 2022-23 Conference League. But after Tuesday, it's also the place where Viking hung three goals on -- and frustrated the hell out of -- Bayern Munich.

You have to take your victories where you can find them early in an eight-game Champions League league phase campaign, where the results aren't incredibly consequential and the surprises are minimal. But Viking vs. Bayern was an absolute blast. Viking ran the "score on your first shot" play -- every team should try that, it works out great for you -- and then went up 2-0 late in the first half. Bayern charged back because Bayern always charge back, but after a gorgeous Konrad Laimer-to-Luis Díaz goal gave the German giants the lead, Michael Olise got a red card, and it pretty visibly flipped the momentum in the match.

Herman Haugen headed in a tying goal over an unsuspecting Alphonso Davies (who probably should have been more suspecting), and Peter Christiansen forced a Jonas Urbig save in extra time. The stats for the game as a whole were one-sided (xG: Bayern 3.3, Viking 0.7), but when the match ended Viking appeared most likely to score next.

The Norwegian style of play might be the most aesthetically pleasing in the world at the moment: a mix of optimism and organization in attack, and a willingness to leave yourself a little exposed in the back. Bodø/Glimt have mastered this style and translated it well to European competitions -- they beat Borussia Dortmund on Wednesday to make it six straight home wins in the Champions League or Champions League qualification -- and Viking's first two Champions League league phase matches have featured 10 combined goals and a draw their fans will be talking about for ages.

I am a total sucker for stories like this.

And while we're celebrating teams that do everything possible to increase the pure entertainment value of the early stages, let's shout out Club Brugge, the watchability kings. So far they've lost 3-2 to Aston Villa and beaten Inter 4-3, and really, Tuesday's win undersold the amount of quality opportunities created: both teams underachieved against xG.

In 18 league phase matches since the start of 2024-25, they've scored multiple goals seven times and allowed multiple goals 10 times. They've won a match while allowing three, and they've drawn a match while scoring three. They are speed horses for this competition, and they are appreciated.

No. 2: Paris Saint-Germain

We're used to PSG taking their time shifting into gear in a given season. Luis Enrique has loads of both stars and incredible teenagers to give minutes to, and he knows he doesn't really have to find or lean on his best 11 until the spring. A few early losses won't exactly hurt them in Ligue 1, and two years ago they won the Champions League despite at one point going winless for four straight league phase matches.

They started this season in a little too much of a funk, however, with a loss to Lens in the Trophée des Champions and just two points in their first three Ligue 1 matches. They were tied for 13th with Le Mans after three league matchdays. That's a bit much.

Luckily, they know how to shift into gear.

In their past five matches on each side of the international break, they've won five matches by a combined 16-5. Enrique's still rotating like crazy -- 20 different guys have started in these five matches -- but PSG's ridiculous depth almost requires him to, and everyone's contributing. Ousmane Dembélé has three goals and four assists in four starts in this span, Ferran Torres has five goals, newcomer Maghnes Akliouche has two goals and an assist, Désiré Doué (who's still only 21, by the way) has a goal and two assists. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia hasn't contributed much, but PSG has still turned into a wrecking ball.

They seemed to have a point to prove Wednesday in Manchester.

Visiting fellow petrol staters Manchester City, who are staring potentially epic penalties in the face, PSG went up 2-0 within 15 minutes thanks to goals from Doué and Dembélé and got a third from midfielder Vitinha before halftime. After Erling Haaland pulled one back for the home team, Akliouche put away an eventual 4-2 win with a goal in the 62nd minute.

City had won eight straight matches in all competitions and had humiliated Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield over the weekend, but PSG basically scored an early-round knockout. The xG figures favored City (2.6 to 1.8), but that can be pretty common when one team takes an early lead. At the time of Vitinha's goal, PSG had attempted eight of the match's 10 shots with a higher volume of touches in the attacking third. They were incredible, and they didn't need long to put the match away.

No. 3: Manchester United

In a way, Manchester United's 2-0 away loss to Atlético Madrid was like just about any other United match in 2026-27, in that the underlying stats that are usually pretty predictive weren't at all. Their xG differential was +0.8 in their 2-0 loss to Hull City to kick off the Premier League season, and in three matches with near-even xGDs, they've lost once with two draws. They're sixth in the Premier League in xG differential but 13th in the table, and at the time of Leny Yoro's 74th-minute red card in Madrid, they trailed 1-0 with a plus-0.4 xGD. (Atleti also ran the "Score on your first shot" play. I'm just saying, it's a great play!) The match turned one-sided after that.

Poor fortune and random, debilitating mistakes are wrecking United's season when they really don't look too poor on paper.

Of course, United's players evidently have their own theory of what's going wrong, one revealed by Lisandro Martínez in postgame interviews. "We did a fantastic season last season and now we expect more from the top, more players to compete, because many teams bring many players as well," he said. "Atlético have an amazing team and they deserved to win today, but I expect more [investment] -- 100%. I expect more from our technical director."

Now, I know that other clubs have invested more than Manchester United in recent years, legally and illegally, and Martinez also made an interesting point about not "[staying] with what you did last season" because opponents always adjust. But despite the Premier League generally losing its mind from the perspective of cumulative transfer fees, I'm never going to see "completely rebuilding your midfield for €173.2 million," as United did this past summer, as a lack of investment or a simple "run it back" approach. United brought in Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans in to address last year's biggest question mark; that's a pretty big change! And they've spent €1.1 billion in transfer fees alone over the past five years. A competent organization should be able to build a perfectly stable team with that.

Even if it's not really a lack of investment, though, United have definitely suffered from a lack of a plan, and it's made competent investment nearly impossible. There's been no ideological consistency in their managerial hires, and their common lineup this season includes two guys who signed or debuted for Louis van Gaal, one for Jose Mourinho, two for Ole Gunnar Solskjær, two for Erik ten Hag, three for Ruben Amorim and one for Michael Carrick. That's a diverse set of influences, and it can't be a surprise when a lack of a plan produces a lack of cohesiveness. But I guess none of what I'm saying is all that original, is it?

No. 4: Serie A

There are nine leagues with multiple Champions League entries this season. Three of them are averaging at least 2.0 points per game among their teams in the field: England's Premier League (2.4), Spain's LaLiga (2.4) and Germany's Bundesliga (2.0). After a perfect 5-for-5 in the wins department in Matchday 1 (followed by a 3-for-3 performance in the Europa League), the Premier League gave away some points this week thanks to the clubs in Manchester.

Four more leagues are averaging at least 1.0 points per game among their teams: France's Ligue 1 (1.5), Portugal's Primeira Liga (1.5), the Netherlands' Eredivisie (1.0) and Norway's Eliteserien (1.0). Hell yeah, Norway. Hanging out with the big boys.

Granted, some of those league successes are coming from one team -- PSG has six of Ligue 1's nine points, and Sporting CP has all six of the Primeira Liga's -- but it's still pretty damn noteworthy that we've gotten this far down the list without mentioning Serie A. After this week's oh-fer, with four losses from four matches, Italian teams now have four points from their first eight matches. Como thumped RB Leipzig in their Champions League home debut in September, and Roma managed a draw against a Fenerbahce team that got blown out by Aston Villa on Wednesday, and that's it.

Now, it's probably not as awful as it seems. Roma played well for 80 minutes against Real Madrid before getting Real Madrid'd at the end for a 4-3 defeat, and Como (lost 3-2 to Feyenoord), Inter (4-3 to Brugge) and Napoli (3-1 to Villarreal) all had at least slightly positive xG differentials, meaning that while their finishing lacked, they were creating equal or better chances than their opponents. But this is still a dire start for a league that has produced just one quarterfinalist in the last three tournaments. (Granted, Inter made the finals in 2025. But that's still it.)

Through two matches each, all four Italian teams have allowed at least two goals from high turnovers, and Roma are one of two teams (along with LASK) to have allowed three. Combined with the fact that the teams are a combined minus-2 in set piece goal differential, you could start to put together a case that Serie A teams aren't really keeping up with the tactical times. But I'll let that one marinate a bit longer before pursuing it further.

Best players of Matchday 2

One thing I like to do if I miss a given match is look at each player's combined xG + xPVA to see who did the most dangerous things in that match. I assume you know xG by now, but xPVA is basically everything else a player did to increase their team's chances of winning (or Expected Point Value), beyond shot attempts - passes, ball recoveries, tackles, et cetera. It's a useful at-a-glance tool, and I figured I'd share the top 15 most dangerous players of Matchday 2.

I enjoy that this is such a mix of expected and unexpected players. It's definitely not a surprise to see Liverpool's Bradley Barcola and Brugge's Nicolo Tresoldi making the list after their respective hat tricks, though Tresoldi evidently produced negative xPVA -- no progressive passes or carries or really anything else, just shots that went into the net. (And hey, if you're only going to do one thing, that's a good one.)

It probably also isn't a surprise that there are two other Brugge players on the list (Carlos Forbs and Romeo Vermant) considering how well they tore apart Inter's midfield. Lautaro had a brace against Brugge, but he could have had so much more: He attempted 12 shots worth 3.0 xG and put nine of those shots on goal. It was honestly one of the most prodigious performances you'll ever see.

There are plenty of familiar names elsewhere -- Erling Haaland, Atleti's Ademola Lookman, Arsenal's Eberechi Eze, Bayern's Luis Diaz -- but among the others let's shout out LASK's Florian Flecker (two goals in 45 minutes against Liverpool), Slavia's Lukás Provod (eight shots worth 1.4 xG, four on target, but somehow no goals) and Fenerbahce's Vedat Muriqi (two shots worth 0.9 xG).

And now, the Power Rankings

This is purely who I would pick if teams were playing this weekend.

1. Barcelona. Two wins and a 9-2 scoring margin thus far. In fact, in all competitions this season they have a perfect 10 wins from 10 matches, with a 43-9 scoring margin. Forty-three! Raphinha has 14 goals and three assists! Lamine Yamal has eight and nine! Fermín López has five and two! Karim Adeyemi has four and two! Anthony Gordon has two and four! Barca are pressing, passing and shooting better than ever, and while we'll have to wait and see if Hansi Flick's high-wire style can win a long series of knockout rounds, there is no question who the best team in Europe is at the moment.

We'll see if we're still saying that after next week: They visit PSG on Tuesday, then host Real Madrid for the first El Clásico of the season on Sunday.

2. PSG. Still only up to sixth in Ligue 1. I doubt they're worried.

3. Arsenal. Methodical and confident.

4. Bayern Munich. I'm not worried about them, but I'm not sure the "allow a goal in the first two minutes every match" approach of the last week is a good thing. (Missing Olise to a red card suspension for next week's Arsenal match stinks.)

5. Manchester City. Crush Liverpool and then get crushed by PSG. A pretty extreme week after a pretty extreme few weeks.

6. Real Madrid. If this isn't a damn "Real Madrid in the Champions League" chart, I don't know what is.

7. Aston Villa. After only one win in their first six matches in all competitions, they're now unbeaten in five, and they've scored 17 goals in the process.

8. Liverpool. It took Bradley Barcola until his seventh match to score in Liverpool red, but a hat trick made up for lost time.

9. Sporting CP. They haven't lost since April, and they've won each of their first two Champions League matches by multiple goals.

10. Atlético Madrid. Five straight wins since the loss to Liverpool.

11. VfB Stuttgart. They were handed a pretty light start -- Viking, at Slovan Bratislava -- and made the most of it with two easy wins. The challenges start with a visit from Atlético next week, but they're already two-thirds of the way toward advancing to the knockouts.

12. Real Betis. Two matches, two 3-2 wins. They drew 67,114 to the Estadio La Cartuja for the win over Porto on Wednesday, and it sounded like 100,000.

13. Borussia Dortmund. After six straight wins before the international break, they have a draw and a loss since. Someone always gets hit by the post-break funk.

14. Manchester United. I'm ranking them 14th because they're basically eighth and 20th at the same time.

15. Club Brugge. Averaging three goals for and three goals against. Hell yeah.

16. Como. They got xG'd against Feyenoord on Wednesday -- three goals allowed from 0.5 xG -- but they still play awfully pretty ball. They belong here.

17. Roma. They're still unbeaten in Serie A play, but their defense isn't holding up in this competition.

18. Villarreal. The Yellow Submarine can't get going in league play, but their finishing was on point against Napoli.

19. Inter Milan. Two one-goal losses isn't the end of the world, but I'd recommend beating Shakhtar next week.

20. RB Leipzig. The reverse Dortmund. RBL had lost three of four before the break and have won two by a combined 7-0 since their return.

21. Bodø/Glimt. Cue the "Chelsea Dagger!"

22. Porto. Their league form (eight matches, eight wins) means I'm not worried about their 0-for-2 start here. But upcoming home matches with PSV and Napoli are pretty big.

23. Lens. They've won only two of their past seven matches, and they have to visit Club Brugge next week.

24. Viking. My new lifelong favorite team.

25. PSV Eindhoven. Ivan Perisic played really well against RB Leipzig on Tuesday, but his failed penalty was a two-point miss in a one-goal loss.

26. Feyenoord. The crowd pop after a Feyenoord home goal is something else.

27. Galatasaray. The home crowd showed out against Barcelona as always, but the home team could only hold on for about 50 minutes.

28. Shakhtar Donetsk. Last year's Conference League semifinal run seems to have carried over. They have four points in two matches, and in their first "home" match at Chelsea's Stamford Bridge, they took the fight to AEK Athens awfully well.

29. Fenerbahçe. The 6-0 loss to Villa was exaggerated -- xG: Villa 3.1, Fenerbahce 1.9 -- but ... woof all the same.

30. Lille. Hey, they were tied with Arsenal for 60 minutes, at least.

31. Napoli. They're eighth in Serie A, and they're 33rd in xG differential after two matches here. Max Allegri was an unambitious hire, and the year sure hasn't started like he hoped.

32. AEK Athens. They had a chance to join the six-point club but could only hold onto a lead against Shakhtar for six minutes.

33. Sabah. They understood the assignment: Their home game with Slavia was probably the most winnable match on the docket, and a crowd of 29,670 showed up to Baki Olimpiya Stadionu to help make sure they won it.

34. LASK. Good: They kept fighting against Liverpool and grabbed a couple of late goals. Bad: They were down 6-1 at the time.

35. Slavia Prague. They're 0-for-2, and they still have to play No. 3, 4 and 7 on this list. Yikes.

36. Slovan Bratislava. They play at LASK on Nov. 3 and host Shakhtar on Dec. 9. If they want points in this competition, those are very important matches.

stories.headline: 2026 WNBA Finals feature record African representation as Golden State, Atlanta chase first title
stories.summary: For the first time in WNBA history, the Finals will feature three players and one executive with African connections, the highest African representation in the championship series dating to the league's inaugural season in 1997.
stories.body:
History will be made when the 2026 WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream tips off this Saturday.

For the first time in league history, the Finals will feature three players and one executive with African connections, the highest African representation in the championship series dating to the league's inaugural season in 1997.

Ghanaian-American general manager Ohemaa Nyanin and Canadian forward Laeticia Amihere, whose parents are Ghanaian, represent Golden State, while on the other side, Atlanta have Mali international Sika Kone and Kenyan center Madina Okot.

The four surpass the previous high of three from 2008, when players Olayinka Sanni (Detroit Shock) and Morenike Atunrase (San Antonio Silver Stars) were on opposing teams, with Mike Ekanem serving as strength and conditioning coach for San Antonio.

All three are of Nigerian heritage, and Sanni even represented Nigeria, winning two silver medals and one bronze across three All Africa Games tournaments.

This year's Finals, which begin Saturday in San Francisco, brings together two franchises seeking their first WNBA championship, with Nyanin's leadership of Golden State's basketball operations introducing an executive dimension to Africa's history in the league.

Appointed the Valkyries' inaugural general manager in May 2024, Nyanin became the first executive of African origin in the WNBA, and has overseen one of the fastest rises by an expansion franchise in WNBA history.

Under her leadership, Golden State became the first WNBA expansion team to qualify for the playoffs in their inaugural season in 2025 and followed that by reaching the Finals in only their second season, another expansion franchise record.

The Valkyries finished the 2026 regular season 32-12 before advancing through the playoffs, including a semifinal victory over defending champion Las Vegas Aces.

Nyanin, who previously served as assistant general manager of the New York Liberty team that reached the 2023 Finals, finished third in voting for the WNBA's 2026 Executive of the Year award.

Golden State's success has also been accompanied by record commercial growth. The franchise became the first professional women's sports team to surpass $100 million in annual revenue and topped the WNBA's franchise valuation rankings at about $1 billion, according to May 2026 estimates by CNBC.

The Valkyries also sold out all 44 regular-season home games across their first two seasons, extending their sellout streak through the playoffs.

Although the commercial achievements fall under the wider franchise leadership, Nyanin has been responsible for constructing the roster that has taken Golden State to the championship series in only their second year, a remarkable accomplishment.

Amihere, who was born in Canada to Ghanaian parents, is one member of that roster. The 6-foot-4 forward won the NCAA championship with South Carolina in 2022, helping coach Dawn Staley's Gamecocks defeat Connecticut in the title game. She made history as a teenager in 2017 when, at 15, she became the first Canadian woman to dunk in a competitive game.

The forward was selected eighth overall by Atlanta Dream in the 2023 WNBA draft and has represented Canada at the Olympic Games, including Tokyo in 2021 and Paris in 2024. Her move to Golden State has now brought her to the WNBA Finals for the first time, adding another milestone to a career that has included college and international basketball success.

On the other side of the floor, Atlanta's African representation comes through two players who have followed different routes to the WNBA.

Kone is an established Mali international who developed through one of Africa's most successful women's basketball programs. She was named MVP of the 2021 FIBA Under-19 Women's Basketball World Cup, after leading Mali to a fourth-place finish, the best result by an African team in the tournament's history.

The now 24-year-old averaged 19.7 points and 14.8 rebounds during that competition and was subsequently selected by New York Liberty with the 29th overall pick in the 2022 WNBA draft.

She has also represented Mali at senior level, including at the Women's AfroBasket, where the country has remained one of the leading challengers to Nigeria's continental dominance.

Her appearance on Atlanta's Finals roster continues Mali's history in the championship series. Hamchetou Maiga-Ba won the championship with Sacramento Monarchs in 2005 and returned to the Finals the following year, when Sacramento lost to Detroit Shock.

Okot, meanwhile, has emerged as Kenya's most prominent women's basketball export. The 6-foot-6 center began playing basketball at 16 after initially pursuing volleyball in Kenya, before moving to the United States and establishing herself in college basketball.

She averaged 11.3 points and 9.6 rebounds at Mississippi State during the 2024-25 season before transferring to South Carolina, where she helped the Gamecocks reach the NCAA championship game in 2026. Okot averaged 12.8 points and 10.6 rebounds in her final college season, recording 22 double-doubles.

Atlanta selected her with the 13th overall pick in the 2026 WNBA draft, making her the first Kenyan player selected in the first round, and only the third in league history, following Josephine Owino, a third-round selection in 2009, and Kenyan-American Olivia Nelson-Ododa, who was drafted in the second round in 2022.

Such is the huge influence that Okot has become in Kenya, that the country's President William Ruto came to watch her play in Atlanta's 83-65 victory over New York Liberty in September.

Ruto, who was in New York for the United Nations General Assembly, attended the game with First Lady Rachel Ruto, NBA Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum and representatives of NBA Africa. Afterward, Ruto and his wife met Okot on the court, took photographs and spoke with her in Swahili.

In her rookie season, she averaged 5.4 points and 3.3 rebounds in 42 regular-season appearances as the Dream returned to the Finals for the first time since 2013.

The presence of the four African-connected figures continues a history dating to the early years of the WNBA. In 2001, just four years after the first Finals, DR Congo's Mwadi Mabika helped the Los Angeles Sparks defeat Charlotte Sting, whose roster included another African, Mozambique's Clarisse Machanguana. Both became the first players of African origin to appear in the Finals.

Mabika returned to the Finals to win a second championship with Los Angeles in 2002, this time against New York Liberty and fellow Congolese player Bernadette Ngoyisa Mudju. But a year later, she was on the other side, as Senegal's Astou Ndiaye-Diatta won the championship with Detroit Shock, defeating Mabika and the Sparks.

Those three consecutive Finals established an early precedent for African-born players appearing on opposing teams in the championship series. In total, players of African origin have been in 15 of the league's 29 previous Finals, with 16 distinct players and 22 total player appearances.

Nigeria, as expected, have had more players in WNBA Finals roster than any other African country, with five including Sanni, Natalia Achonwa, Ogwumike, Liz Cambage and Ezi Magbegor.

Los Angeles have also won more championships with African-connected players than any other franchise, claiming three through Mabika's two titles and Nigerian-American forward Ogwumike's championship in 2016.

Ogwumike, who won the league's MVP award that season, scored the decisive basket in Game 5 against Minnesota Lynx and returned to the Finals in 2017, but was second time unlucky when Los Angeles lost the title to Minnesota.

Mabika remains the most successful African-born player in league history, with two titles from three Finals appearances. Eight players of African origin have been WNBA champions, for a total of nine titles.

These include Seattle Storm's Magbegor, whose family has Nigerian roots, in 2020; Senegal-born Astou Ndour-Fall with Chicago Sky in 2021; and Nyara Sabally, whose father is Gambian, with New York Liberty in 2024, along with Hamchetou Maiga-Ba, and Olayinka Sanni.

The African connection also extended beyond the playing roster. Ekanem's involvement with San Antonio in 2008 helped establish the previous high for African representation in a Finals series, while Nigerian origin athletic trainer Michelle Anumba was part of the Las Vegas Aces' back-to-back championship teams in 2022 and 2023.

This year's championship series adds the front office into that history, with Nyanin overseeing the basketball operations of a Golden State team attempting to win a title in only their second season.

Atlanta, who have lost three previous Finals appearances in 2010, 2011 and 2013, are hoping to heal from the trauma of those losses by putting the memory behind them to claim their first championship in franchise history.

The series opens on Saturday at Chase Center, with one franchise guaranteed to win its first WNBA title. But more importantly for Africa, whichever team wins that first chip, there will be at least two Africans on the podium when that final buzzer goes.

stories.headline: AFL trade and free agency grades - Every club's report card from the 2026 transfer period
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL trade and free agency period is over. Some teams improved, some stagnated, and others, well, got worse. Here's how every team fared over the last two weeks.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL trade and free agency period is complete. Some teams improved, some have stagnated, and others, well, seemed to have gotten worse.

READ: Every player move from the 2026 off-season

Here's how every team fared over the last two weeks:

Adelaide
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Jordon Butts, Luke Pedlar

2026 draft selections: 15, 32, 35, 43, 56, 92

I'm not sure what the Crows' gameplan was this trade and free agency period, but it's fair to say the club sat on its hands and did next to nothing. Losing key defender Jordon Butts to the Bulldogs obviously weakens them, while just one draft selection inside the top 30 is unlikely to provide much immediate support. Adelaide's list profile remains fine, and maybe they will surprise us all in 2027, but you just get the sense so many other clubs have passed them by over the last two weeks.

Grade: F

Brisbane
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Lachie Neale, Sam Marshall, Will McLachlan, Keidean Coleman

2026 draft selections: 21, 27, 28, 45, 79, 97

The Lions were the biggest winners of last year's off-season (and season!), but this year was a different story. All year it seemed a formality they would lose the services of dual Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale, who ultimately signed with Collingwood as a free agent. They also waved goodbye to Keidean Coleman and Sam Marshall, two players who had struggled to crack the best 23 of late. No picks inside the top 20 would be concerning for 17 other clubs, but the Lions still have so much young talent at their disposal and are primed to challenge again in 2027.

Grade: C-

Carlton
Incoming: Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield

Outgoing: Hudson O'Keeffe, Flynn Riley

2026 draft selections: 13, 18, 31, 50, 61, 72, 90

The Blues addressed two areas of weakness this off-season. The addition of free agent Joel Amartey provides spearhead Harry McKay with a stable forward line partner, while the Lachie Whitfield signing offers run, experience, and a kick-first option off halfback, the perfect piece to fit into Josh Fraser's system. Carlton really didn't give up much to land Whitfield, either. And barring Essendon taking a stab at talented father-son prospect Cody Walker with pick No. 1, the club has also ensured it has enough draft capital to match any bids that will come for him.

Grade: A

Collingwood
Incoming: Lachie Neale, Jesse Hogan, Flynn Riley

Outgoing: Scott Pendlebury

2026 draft selections: 11, 30, 67, 68, 70, 88

The Magpies had been crying out for a true inside midfielder, and they landed arguably the best in the competition in Lachie Neale. The two-time Brownlow Medal winner is an elite ball winner and clearance player, and should perfectly complement superstar Nick Daicos. Collingwood also signed Jesse Hogan, a man that won the Coleman Medal just two years ago, and gave up virtually nothing for him. The loss of champion Scott Pendlebury obviously stings, but you have to feel this club is in a stronger position now than it was two weeks ago.

Grade: A

Essendon
Incoming: Jack Bowes, Keidean Coleman

Outgoing: Zach Merrett, Jordan Ridley

2026 draft selections: 1, 17, 25, 80

Former skipper Zach Merrett finally got his wish of a fresh start at the Hawks, while fellow experienced player Jordan Ridley also departs the club for the Cats. The additions of Jack Bowes and Keidean Coleman are fine, but are either going to be difference makers in a side that's been languishing at the bottom of the ladder for several years? I'm not so sure. The only saving grace for the Bombers is that they hold pick No. 1. They simply have to make the most of that selection.

Grade: D

Fremantle
Incoming: Dom Bedendo

Outgoing: Nathan O'Driscoll

2026 draft selections: 19, 40, 60, 63, 78, 96

The Dockers were incredibly quiet during the trade and free agency window, but that's not exactly a bad thing. Remember, if not for Will Ashcroft and Logan Morris, Fremantle win the 2026 premiership. There was absolutely no reason for the Dockers to panic and overpay for someone after their Grand Final heartbreak, instead, this club, with its plethora of youth and talent, should feel as if it can contend for years to come. Trust the process and go again in 2027.

Grade: C

Geelong
Incoming: Toby Greene, Jordan Ridley, Rowan Marshall

Outgoing: Jack Bowes

2026 draft selections: 36, 57, 62, 75, 93

Every year the Cats just find a way to bring big names through the door, and 2026 was no exception. Rowan Marshall was tipped to join 12 months ago and finally makes the move from St Kilda to bolster the club's ruck stocks. Toby Greene adds class, experience, and unrivalled goal-kicking nous to the forward line. Jordan Ridley is a stable and still wildly underrated defensive asset. The best part? To land this trio the club only had to give up midfield depth piece Jack Bowes, and some draft capital. They won't be much of a feature at the upcoming draft, but they don't have to be. These Cats are in win-now mode.

Grade: A

Gold Coast Suns
Incoming: Scott Pendlebury, Aidan Schubert, Sam Butler

Outgoing: Ben King

2026 draft selections: 8, 85

Scott Pendlebury might be a champion of the game, but there's no denying the Suns just got worse. The addition of 38-year-old Pendlebury doesn't outweigh the seismic loss of spearhead Ben King, a man who has booted 230 goals over the last four seasons. How do they replace him? Perhaps it's the incoming Aidan Schubert, but he's years away from having a real impact. Making matters worse, it seems Brownlow medallist Matt Rowell is likely to request a trade back to Victoria at the end of next season. This club is in a real precarious spot right now. A penny for Christian Petracca's thoughts...

Grade: C-

GWS Giants
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Toby Greene, Kieren Briggs, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield

2026 draft selections: 9, 20, 26, 59, 77, 86

Just two years ago Toby Greene, Kieren Briggs, Jesse Hogan, and Lachie Whitfield were probably four of the Giants' most important players. None of them remain at the club after an action-packed trade and free agency window, with GWS instead opting to clear out and trust the youth underneath. It's a move that will either make the Giants look like geniuses or total fools, but even those who are incredibly bullish about the approach would concede there is likely to be some pain on the immediate horizon.

Grade: D

Hawthorn
Incoming: Zach Merrett, Ben King, Josh Goater

Outgoing: Finn Maginness, Aidan Schubert, Sam Butler, Bodie Ryan

2026 draft selections: 29, 37, 71, 94

The Hawks should probably be the 2027 flag favourites after a whirlwind two weeks that's seen them finally land former Essendon skipper Zach Merrett, as well as Ben King. Merrett adds depth, experience, and A-grade ball use to Hawthorn's midfield group, while King provides a focal point in attack, taking the burden off the ageing Jack Gunston. Sure, Hawthorn gave up some depth, but their best 23 has improved out of sight and they still have draft collateral over the next few years to ensure talent keeps coming through the door.

Grade: A+

Melbourne
Incoming: Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, Bodie Ryan

Outgoing: Jack Viney, Trent Rivers

2026 draft selections: 4, 14, 48, 52

Just about everyone panicked when the Demons farewelled premiership heroes Christian Petracca and Clayton Oliver last year, and look how that turned out. This club seems to have a plan for the future and it isn't prepared to compromise on what it wants. Melbourne has nailed its draft picks in recent times and with selections four and 14 this year, you'd expect two more highly talented prospects to join the ranks. Who knows if Zane Duursma will work out, but they've landed him for a fraction of what the Kangaroos gave up at the draft three years ago. It's a low risk punt worth taking.

Grade: C

North Melbourne
Incoming: Nick Blakey

Outgoing: Zane Duursma, Josh Goater

2026 draft selections: 33, 49, 66, 74, 84

Credit to the Kangaroos, they finally landed a big name. The only problem is I'm not sure Nick Blakey is the superstar many are claiming. There's no doubt Blakey will add drive and dash off halfback, but is he the player you look to in the closing stages of a tight game? North also gave up a truckload of future draft capital to get him through the door which will hurt them in the coming years. And then there's the Zane Duursma fiasco. Losing a player the club invested pick No. 4 in just three years ago is an unmitigated disaster. With no selections inside the top 30 this year, it will be a rare draft without the Roos being a major player.

Grade: C+

Port Adelaide
Incoming: Luke Pedlar

Outgoing: Zak Butters

2026 draft selections: 7, 12, 22, 24, 34, 46, 65

You're never going to feel great when a player of Zak Butters' class and calibre walks out the door, but the silver lining for Port Adelaide is that Dougie Cochrane should be set to walk back in. The academy talent is the consensus best player in the upcoming draft and the Power are in a position to match any bids on their man. Expect Port to be heavily involved in the draft over the next couple of years as they look to rebuild around the likes of Cochrane, Connor Rozee, and Jason Horne-Francis.

Grade: B

Richmond
Incoming: Kieren Briggs, Nathan O'Driscoll

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 2, 5, 44, 81

The Tigers found Toby Nankervis' successor in Kieren Briggs, who crosses from the Giants as a free agent. That's a nice win. Nathan O'Driscoll was unable to find a place in Fremantle's best team of late but should receive far more opportunity in the black and yellow jumper in 2027. Richmond has two more picks inside the top five, though they are likely to be shuffled down a few spots with bid matching on Dougie Cochrane and Cody Walker, and they simply must nail them. Even still, this side will remain incredibly young in 2027.

Grade: C

St Kilda
Incoming: Sam Marshall

Outgoing: Rowan Marshall

2026 draft selections: 10, 16, 41, 51, 69, 87

The Saints went all-in last year, signing Tom De Koning, Jack Silvagni, Liam Ryan, and Sam Flanders. They weren't nearly as busy this off-season, and few expected them to be. Long-time ruck Rowan Marshall departs the club for the Cats, while Sam Marshall joins and should bolster their midfield stocks. Outside of that, St Kilda will be hoping to cash in with their two first round draft selections. If not, it could spell the end of Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera's tenure. This team wouldn't want to be starting 2027 slowly...

Grade: C

Sydney Swans
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Joel Amartey, Nick Blakey

2026 draft selections: 6, 38, 39, 47, 54, 76, 95

Two best 23 players departed the Swans this past fortnight with halfback Nick Blakey being traded to the Kangaroos and key forward Joel Amartey signing with the Blues as a free agent. Don't forget, Callum Mills is unlikely to suit up for the entire year after suffering an ACL injury during this year's finals campaign. That's three best 23 players to replace! Who knows what's happening with Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner? Swans fans will be praying for a hit with pick No. 6 at the upcoming draft to soften the blow.

Grade: C-

West Coast Eagles
Incoming: Jack Viney, Trent Rivers

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 3, 23, 58, 64, 73, 82

It's clear the Eagles don't want to take the same approach as the Tigers and rely solely on the kids. Instead, they're continuing to add experienced pieces around their young talent in an effort to ease the rebuild and avoid a nosedive in morale. Jack Viney and Trent Rivers add premiership experience to the club and they haven't had to give up too much to get them. West Coast will feature prominently at November's draft with pick No. 3, 23, as well as a compensation pick in the likely scenario that the club's first selection is pushed back by a bid.

Grade: C+

Western Bulldogs
Incoming: Jordon Butts, Finn Maginness, Hudson O'Keeffe, Zak Butters

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 42, 53, 55, 83, 89, 91

The Bulldogs now possess the most dynamic midfield trio in the game with Zak Butters joining skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards in the red, white, and blue. It's a marquee signing for Luke Beveridge's team that simply has to put them into premiership contention. Jordon Butts also joins the club and will bolster what's traditionally been a weaker defensive unit. Don't forget about key forward star Sam Darcy, who will return from a season-ending ACL injury.

Grade: A+

stories.headline: Why is Max Verstappen racing in GT World Challenge? Schedule, how to watch latest non-F1 event
stories.summary: Max Verstappen has made no secret of his enjoyment of racing outside Formula 1, and the four-time world champion is set to take on his latest motorsport challenge.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen has made no secret of his enjoyment of racing outside Formula 1, and the four-time world champion is set to take on his latest racing challenge.

There is little time for rest for the Dutchman, who heads to Portimão to compete in the latest GT World Challenge event, sandwiched between two F1 triple-headers.

The one-off event will also feature some of the best drivers in the world, including World Endurance Championship title winner Nicki Thiim, nine-time MotoGP world champion Valentino Rossi, who competes for BMW in the World Endurance Championship, and Ferrari development driver Arthur Leclerc.

Here's everything you need to know about the 10th and final round of the GT World Challenge.

- Max Verstappen steps in for GT race at Portimão amid two F1 triple-headers

- When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

Why is Verstappen racing this weekend?

Verstappen has been one of the biggest critics around F1's controversial new regulations, calling them "anti-racing."

Things are, however, on the up after he took his first victory this season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, before following it up with a dominant win in Singapore, as Red Bull continue to thrive with its upgraded package.

Despite finding success in F1, the simple reason why he's back to GT racing this weekend is due to some of Verstappen Racing's usual drivers not being available to compete. Dani Juncadella and Jules Gounon have a World Endurance Championship calendar clash with the Portuguese round on Oct. 18.

Verstappen decided to step in and will be racing alongside Ben Barnicoat and Chris Lulham.

"I know that two of my drivers won't be part of the line-up, so two other drivers need to step in and I'm looking forward to it," Verstappen said.

"It's going to be a busy seven weeks, but we'll do it and I enjoy it anyway. So, yeah. Let's see what we can do there."

It's set to be a busy weekend with the GT2 European Series, GT4 European Series and McLaren Trophy Europe all set to crown their champions.

The 29-year-old will be back in his Red Bull a week later in Texas for F1's United States Grand Prix, where he will target a third win in a row.

GT World Challenge schedule
All times in BST

Thursday, October 15

Official Paid Test Session 1: 11.50 a.m.

Bronze test: 5.40 p.m.

Friday, October 16

Free Practice 1: 8.45 a.m.

Qualifying: 5.55 p.m. - 7.05 p.m.

Saturday, October 17

Race: 5 p.m. - 8 p.m.

How to watch

The GT World Challenge will be streamed on the official GT World YouTube Channel or via the GT World Challenge Europe website.

Portimão Circuit

Built in the Algarve region in southern Portugal, the circuit is a mix of fast and slow corners which features some extreme elevation changes.

There are overtaking opportunities, but the 4.653km track is considered challenging with its 16 corners.

It's so popular that it's returning to the F1 calendar in 2027 and 2028. The race next year will take the place of the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort.

Weather forecast

The weather forecast for the race in Portimão is set to be sunny with a gentle breeze, with highs of 27°C on Thursday through to race day on Saturday.

Verstappen's other racing ventures

During his debut GT3 race in the Nürburgring Endurance Series in September last year he landed a stunning victory in a Ferrari 296 entered by Emil Frey Racing.

In March, he drove a Mercedes-AMG GT3 through Verstappen Racing in the preliminary NLS2 race which is a four-hour endurance race. He won the race but was later disqualified over a tyre error.

A few months later he competed in one of motor racing's toughest endurance tests -- the iconic Nürburgring 24-hour race under Verstappen Racing driving a Mercedes-AMG GT3 Evo.

He came close to ticking a dream off his list, but his car suffered a driveshaft issue with three hours of the race remaining.

Verstappen more recently took part in a more lighthearted challenge where he took on 100 creators and sports personalities in go-karts starting from the back of the grid. Nobody was sure how the race would unravel at the custom-built track at Silverstone, but he ended up passing every single driver to lead the race after 35 minutes.

stories.headline: Michael 'Venom' Page: UFC's Dana White 'never really a fan of me'
stories.summary: Michael "Venom" Page has said that his relationship with UFC president Dana White was "nonexistent."
stories.body:
Michael "Venom" Page said that his relationship with UFC president Dana White was "nonexistent" in an exclusive interview with ESPN on Tuesday.

Page joined the UFC in 2023 with his stock at an all-time high after serving as the face of Bellator courtesy of a series of exciting stoppages with his unique freestyle striking style.

But he couldn't replicate that in the UFC with a run of impressive, albeit uninspiring, decision wins in the promotion, along with a solitary defeat to Ian Machado-Garry, leading to the conclusion of his six-fight contract.

White confirmed in September that the UFC would not pursue another deal, and Page announced this week that his next venture is with KSI's Misfits boxing in a "multi-fight, multi-year agreement." And reflecting on his time in the promotion, Page said he felt that White was "never really a fan of me from the beginning."

"Literally nonexistent [relationship with White]," Page told ESPN. "I think we've had a couple of very brief conversations, very, very brief. [Chief business officer Hunter Campbell] was the person that I spoke with quite regularly. I was thankful for him. ... It was him that signed me. It was more Hunter that was the person that was like, 'Look, I want you in the UFC.'

"So I feel like Dana White's never really been a fan of me from the beginning, or I think it came from somebody else. And because I also didn't deliver it in the way he wanted me to deliver, I get he didn't care. You can kind of tell from the announcement, he didn't really make anything of it. He just announced me on the card as if I've always been a fighter there and people were kind of like, 'Wait, what?'

"So I feel like potentially, just based on how he behaves, I'm speculating here, that potentially he wasn't necessarily a fan of mine. And then on top of that, I didn't give him what he wanted as well. So yeah, there was no real relationship with Dana."

UFC didn't respond to ESPN's request for comment.

Page's UFC career wrapped up with a decision win over Nursulton Ruziboev amid boos from a partisan crowd in Paris last month.

Misfits wasn't the only promotion Page spoke to when looking at steps after the UFC with Jake Paul's Most Valuable Promotions among those interested in the Brit. Page said that a move to MVP, who has recently acquired MMA promotion PFL, was considered, but the timing wasn't right.

"Obviously that [MVP] was probably one of the things at the top of the list. But they just weren't in the right place right now," he said. "It wasn't the right timing more than anything. It wasn't just a financial thing, but it wasn't the right timing for them."

stories.headline: 'All love': All Blacks inspiring NZ's Rugby League World Cup tilt
stories.summary: Buoyed by a visit from their All Blacks brothers, Stacey Jones's ambitious Kiwis are out to open the rugby league World Cup with a bang by completing a memorable New Zealand double over Australia.
stories.body:
Buoyed by a visit from their All Blacks brothers, Stacey Jones's ambitious Kiwis are out to open the rugby league World Cup with a bang by completing a memorable New Zealand double over Australia.

Five days after the All Blacks crushed the Wallabies 50-19 to clinch the Bledisloe Cup for a 23rd straight year, the Kiwis and Kangaroos clash in a trans-Tasman blockbuster in Sydney on Thursday night to kick off the global showpiece.

Eight ABs, including superstar winger Will Jordan and playmaker Cam Roigard, cast aside the cross-code rivalry to drop into New Zealand's captain's run on Wednesday and throw their support behind Jones's side.

"It's just all love and supporting each other and hopefully we can go watch their game on Saturday too, so it's pretty special," New Zealand captain James Fisher-Harris said.

"How dominant and how they go about their business and represent New Zealand, there's a lot of things that they do that we look up to so yeah, it's pretty cool."

Leading what he believes is "potentially" the best Kiwi forward pack ever, Fisher-Harris says "the plan" is to lift the World Cup and, like the Warriors, continue to inspire a whole new generation of rugby league players back in their homeland just like the 2008 winners did.

"When they won in 2008, I was watching Blairy (Adam Blair) and that, (Nathan) Cayless and obviously Benji (Marshall), so that made me want to go down this path," the enforcer said.

"So hopefully we can do something like that. When you are successful like that, it gets you motivated and you want to play for a certain team or a certain code.

"So that's the plan anyways, to be successful in this World Cup."

Behind the monster pack will be Kayln Ponga for the first time after the talismanic fullback, at 28, opted to represent his parents' homeland.

"He's playing pretty good right about now," Fisher-Harris said of Ponga, who led Newcastle on their magical run from seventh to a 19-18 grand final loss to the Sydney Roosters.

"But it's not just his playing ability, it's his leadership and he's been in the game for a while now.

"He's won a few things but it looks like he's pretty keen to get in that black and white jersey."

Coach Stacey Jones also believes Australia's loss is very much New Zealand's gain.

"For the Knights this year and particularly the back end of the season, he carried them to a grand final," Jones said.

"Obviously had a lot of support around him, but he's got a lot of confidence in his game at the moment and we're just lucky that we've got him on our side."
